title: The right bank of US 163
summary: USGS bare-earth elevations now shape the nearer highway banks at construction time when a qualified survey is cached. The ordinary driving mesh and its physics collider share the measured shoulder. A protected strip preserves road grades and intersections, and independent site surveys have priority.
measurement: Against 1,502 off-grid locations from the original 1 m Utah DEM, mean road-relative height error fell from 1.33 m without the survey and 1.08 m with the former bank solver to 0.48 m. A 120 m stock Miata run kept all four wheel contacts for 662 physics ticks. A West Virginia holdout improved from 0.39 to 0.36 m. In the matched view the right bank gets closer to the reference, but the left turnout gets farther away in color.
credit: Photograph by Awinda, April 30, 2023. The cropped comparison is licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. The reference camera uses the published GPS and a landmark-aligned 233.2° view; the iPhone recorded 242.1°. The earlier comparison uses fixed afternoon light. The new comparison uses the reference-date lighting. The measured terrain uses public-domain USGS 3DEP data and OpenStreetMap road geometry.

Enlarged engine crops and a cross section 150 m up the highway. The lines show height relative to the center of the mapped road. The safety margin preserves the closest shoulder.
Same camera and historical daylight. The new survey mesh lifts both cut banks into the driver’s view. The foreground still lacks the source rock cover and individual plants.
